title: Find out why Ask sometimes waits five minutes for the local model and makes nothing
goal: During one eval run, three of 42 requests sat on Working for the whole five minutes because the model on this Mac never answered, and the person would get nothing at the end. Find out whether Ask or the model runner is stuck, and make a stalled request end quickly with a plain message instead of spinning.
notes: Seen 2026-10-20 in the held-out baseline (.ask-eval/held-out-runs/20261021-010309-ask-held-out): pose-cat-yawning (18:19-18:24), pose-person-waving (18:25-18:30) and scene-squirrel-acorn-stump (18:39-18:44) each ended with the walk step '[8 waitFor] FAILED: askPhase("ran|stopped") did not happen within 300.0s' and Ask's trace stopping at '0.0s asking the model' (ask.trace in ask-walk/log.json). Other cases in between answered in about 8 s. curl -s localhost:11434/api/ps afterwards listed qwen3:30b plus a second model loaded, so contention for Ollama is one suspect; not reproduced on demand. AskLocalModel.swift sets timeoutInterval 300 and resource timeout 600 on the chat call. Not filed p1 because not reproduced; the eval counts these as nothing made.
acceptance: The cause of the stalls is named, with the command and output that show it (the model runner busy with another request, a model being loaded, or Ask's own call)
A request the model has not started answering within a reasonable time (measure it; today Ask waits 300 seconds) stops with a short message and changes nothing
The eval's held-out run has no case that ends still planning

claimed by go loop

Cause named: the model was answering throughout. For all 18 eval stalls I could match to a server log (2026-10-23 to 11-09) the server worked the whole 300 s: 7 to 24 planning turns (pricing 2026-11-04 04:38Z: 10 tasks, longest gap 7.7 s), or the Mac slowed to a sixth of its speed (heart 2026-11-08 18:10Z: 5 t/s writing vs 33). The trace 'stopped at asking the model' was read by the walk at the Send press (3 s in); since 282341071 (2026-11-10) a timed-out wait records the whole trace. Commands: python3 /tmp/stallcheck/match.py over every done.json with 'did not happen within' in .ask-eval/runs (climb only), matched to ~/Library/Caches/Photonz/ask-walk-server/log and the probe's ask-model log.

Measured the quiet time: across 26,849 server tasks in every server log on this Mac, a working server logged progress at most 37 s apart (contention), 14.2 s at the 99.9th percentile. Chose 90 s. Chose a request deadline (no round after 240 s, cut at 270 s, offer what was planned) over raising the eval limit because a person should not wait past five minutes either and AskMotionLook already holds the request to five minutes.

Verified on the probe with the real model: ask-ends-inside-its-time-walk (askSeconds 60) cut the round at 54.6 s and landed the 2 texts planned, row 'Stopped after Pricing Subtitle'. Reproduced a frozen server by kill -STOP on the probe's llama-server mid-request: Ask said 'Ask's model went quiet. Try again.' at 117.7 s (90 s after its last news), changed nothing, server stopped. Committed ab842bf49. Now running the held-out set on it in resumed chunks for acceptance 3.

Cause named: the model never went quiet; in all 18 matched stalls its server log shows it answering for the whole 300 s (7 to 24 planning turns, or a Mac slowed 6x), and the trace only looked stopped because the walk read it 3 s in. Try again.', changing nothing.
